title: Cross-language Java: numeric promotion and timestamp precision can break contracts
summary: The literal Java↔JMS↔ooRexx run found two failures that unit-shaped reasoning missed: a conditional expression promoted integer JSON tokens to Double and changed canonical signed JSON (`50000`→`50000.0`), and Java Instant nanosecond output exceeded the ooRexx DateTime input shape. The fix was explicit numeric branches and UTC timestamps capped at millisecond precision.
invariants: Do not assume Java numeric-expression promotion preserves a wire representation.
Canonical signatures are over the exact cross-language representation, not the programmer's intended numeric category.
Timestamp precision is part of an interop contract when the receiver parser constrains it.
Stable command/idempotency identity must not depend on sub-millisecond timestamp precision.
